title.en: Yoga for daily life: paths and Ashtanga

text.en: At a 10-day yoga summer camp children listed all they enjoyed - playing, painting, stories, healthy food, asanas, helping others, feeding animals. The mentor smiled: When we do anything with joy in our hearts and calmness in our minds, it becomes yoga.

Yoga is more than asanas. Every action done with awareness, happiness and dedication is yoga.
There are paths of yoga. In Grade 5 we learn three: Karma Yoga (action), Gyana Yoga (knowledge) and Bhakti Yoga (devotion).
Karma Yoga is doing our work with honesty, love and effort without expecting a reward. Jadav Molai Payeng planted trees on a bare sandbar in Majuli, Assam, after seeing snakes die without shade.
Gyana Yoga is the path of knowledge, curiosity and asking questions. Swami Chinmayananda is regarded as a great Gyana yogi of modern times.
Bhakti Yoga is loving God with a pure heart and seeing God in everyone. Sanandana's pure bhakti to his Guru Adi Shankaracharya earned him the name Padmapada, 'the one whose feet are supported by lotuses'.
Ashtanga Yoga has eight limbs: Yama, Niyama, Asana, Pranayama, Pratyahara, Dharana, Dhyana and Samadhi, written by Patanjali in the Yoga Sutras over 2000 years ago.
This year we learn Asteya (not taking what is not ours), Swadhyaya (self-study) and Pratyahara (mastery over the senses), like the qualities of a good student. In the story, Kavya returns Adya's hair clip and feels light, like a burden is gone.

requiredIdeas.en: Do duties with honesty and love

points.en: Yoga is any action with joy, awareness and calm.
Three paths: Karma, Gyana and Bhakti.
Asteya is not taking what is not ours.
